9	# Pre-rename cleanup criteria — CL-000 epic
10	
11	This doc defines the objective criteria the CL-002 / CL-003 / CL-004 inventory
12	beads use to classify candidates, the evidence the CL-005 / CL-006 / CL-007
13	deletion beads must cite, and the rollback expectations for any deletion or
14	archival landed before the Fizeau rename.
15	
16	The goal of CL-000 is not to clean up the codebase in general — it is to
17	shrink the rename surface so FZ-001 operates on the smallest practical set of
18	files. Anything outside that scope is out-of-scope for this epic.
19	
20	## Decision: delete / archive / keep
21	
22	Every candidate identified by an inventory bead **must** be assigned exactly
23	one of three classifications. The classification determines what the
24	corresponding deletion bead is allowed to do.
25	
26	### Delete
27	
28	A candidate may be classified `delete` only if **all** of the following hold:
29	
30	1. **No active references.** No production code, test, build script, CI
31	   workflow, generated asset, docs page, or CLI path imports, includes,
32	   embeds, or links to it.
33	2. **No external entry point.** It is not a public API surface, exported
34	   symbol used by an external consumer (binaries built from `cmd/`,
35	   published packages, install-script targets), or documented user-facing
36	   command.
37	3. **No load-bearing history role.** It is not the canonical source for a
38	   shipped behavior whose history future maintainers will need to read
39	   (see "Historical artifacts" below — those are `keep`, not `delete`).
40	4. **Either dead or duplicated.** It is one of:
41	   - **Dead**: no callers, no readers, no consumers (orphan code, dangling
42	     fixture, stale cast file, obsolete profile, generated artifact whose
43	     generator is gone).
44	   - **Duplicated**: another file/package supersedes it, the supersession
45	     is documented (commit message, ADR, prior research note), and no
46	     references still point at the old version.
47	
48	Any candidate that meets `delete` should be removed outright — `git`
49	history preserves it, so archival adds noise without value.
50	
51	### Archive
52	
53	A candidate is `archive` if it has **historical value** but **no active
54	references**. Archive means: move into a clearly-marked archival location
55	(e.g. `docs/research/archive/`, `docs/helix/<phase>/archive/`), not delete.
56	
57	Archive when:
58	
59	- The artifact records a decision, experiment, or baseline that future
60	  readers will plausibly need to consult, **and**
61	- It has no active references (no one links to it, imports it, or runs
62	  it), **and**
63	- Leaving it in the active tree would mislead a reader into thinking it is
64	  current.
65	
66	If an artifact has active references, fix the references first or
67	classify it as `keep` — do not archive something that is still linked to.
68	
69	### Keep
70	
71	A candidate is `keep` if any of the following hold:
72	
73	- It has at least one active reference (import, link, CLI invocation,
74	  generated-asset dependency, test fixture lookup).
75	- It is in a non-delete category (see next section).
76	- The inventory cannot conclusively prove it is dead within the time
77	  budget of the inventory bead. **Default to `keep` when uncertain** —
78	  the rename is the deadline-driven work, not the cleanup.
79	
80	A `keep` classification with old naming is fine; renames will pick those
81	up. The point of CL-000 is only to shrink the surface, not to scrub it.
82	
83	## Non-delete categories (explicit)
84	
85	The following categories are **never** classified `delete` or `archive` by
86	the CL beads, even if they reference old naming or look stale. They are
87	either historical (touch only with a separate, well-justified bead) or
88	they belong to a different epic:
89	
90	| Category | Why it is `keep` here |
91	|---|---|
92	| `CHANGELOG.md` entries | Historical record of shipped behavior; renames are appended, never rewritten. |
93	| `docs/helix/**` retrospectives, ADRs, design notes for shipped work | HELIX phase artifacts — historical decisions, not active docs. May reference old names. |
94	| Git-tracked release notes, milestone summaries | Same: historical. |
95	| `.ddx/beads.jsonl`, `.ddx/executions/**` | DDx execution evidence; not source. |
96	| Third-party vendored code (if any appears under `internal/` or via submodules) | Out of scope for CL-000. |
97	| Files that are touched only by FZ-* beads (the rename itself) | The rename handles them; CL beads must not. |
98	| Anything flagged by an open bead outside `area:rename, kind:cleanup` | Belongs to that bead's epic. |
99	
100	If an inventory bead believes one of these categories should be revisited,
101	it must file a follow-up bead rather than reclassify it.
102	
103	## Required evidence by candidate type
104	
105	Each row in an inventory bead's table **must** cite the evidence
106	appropriate to its candidate type. Inventories without this evidence are
107	not acceptable input for the deletion beads.
108	
109	### Go code (CL-002 → CL-005)
110	
111	For every Go package, file, exported symbol, or sub-package proposed for
112	deletion, the inventory must cite all of:
113	
114	| Evidence | Concrete form |
115	|---|---|
116	| Package builds and tests today | `go list ./...` includes it; `go test ./...` passes on `HEAD`. |
117	| No importers in this repo | `rg -n '"<full/import/path>"'` returns no results outside the package itself, or `go list -f '{{.ImportPath}}: {{.Imports}}' ./... \| rg <pkg>` is empty. |
118	| No symbol references | `rg -n '\b<ExportedSymbol>\b'` returns no callers outside the package's own files. |
119	| Not a binary entry point | Not under `cmd/<name>`, not referenced by `Makefile`, not referenced by `install.sh` or any CI workflow. |
120	| Tests still pass after a local removal trial | `go test ./...` and `go vet ./...` pass with the candidate removed (record the command and result; do not commit the trial). |
121	| Lint clean | `golangci-lint run ./...` (or whichever lint Makefile uses) passes after trial removal. |
122	
123	For duplicate supersession, additionally cite:
124	
125	- The superseding package/file path.
126	- The commit, ADR, or research note documenting the supersession.
127	- `rg` evidence that all references now point at the superseder.
128	
129	### Docs (CL-003 → CL-006)
130	
131	For every doc file, page, or section proposed for deletion or archival,
132	the inventory must cite:
133	
134	| Evidence | Concrete form |
135	|---|---|
136	| Inbound link search | `rg -n '<filename>' docs/ README.md AGENTS.md CONTRIBUTING.md website/` returns the expected set (typically: only the file itself and known historical mentions). |
137	| External link search | `rg -n '<filename>'` across the whole repo returns no hits in code, scripts, CI, or generated-site sources outside the docs tree. |
138	| Website inclusion check | If the docs are rendered (e.g. `website/`, Hugo content), confirm whether the file is built into the site (`rg <filename> website/content/` etc.). A built page is `keep` until the site stops including it. |
139	| Classification | `active` (current docs), `historical` (HELIX/changelog/ADR), or `superseded` (point at the replacement). |
140	| For `superseded` candidates: replacement | File path or URL of the doc that replaces it; `rg` evidence that consumers now reference the replacement. |
141	
142	`historical` always classifies as `keep`. Only `superseded` (with a
143	replacement) and `active-but-stale-and-orphaned` (no inbound links, no
144	website inclusion, no replacement needed because it documented a removed
145	behavior) classify as `delete` or `archive`.
146	
147	### Scripts, fixtures, cast files, sessions, profiles, assets, testdata (CL-004 → CL-007)
148	
149	For every script, fixture, cast file, JSONL session, benchmark profile,
150	generated asset, or `testdata/` entry proposed for deletion, the
151	inventory must cite:
152	
153	| Evidence | Concrete form |
154	|---|---|
155	| No script references | `rg -n '<basename>' scripts/ Makefile lefthook.yml .github/` returns no callers. |
156	| No code references | `rg -n '<basename>'` across `*.go`, `*.ts`, `*.js`, `*.py` returns no readers. |
157	| No CI references | `rg -n '<basename>' .github/workflows/` is empty. |
158	| No fixture-loader reference | For `testdata/` entries: `rg -n '<basename>' .` shows no test loads it (`os.Open`, `embed.FS`, `filepath.Join("testdata", …)`). |
159	| Not regenerable from a live generator | If the file is generated, the generator either no longer exists or the regenerated artifact is not consumed. Cite the generator path or its absence. |
160	| Targeted re-run passes | After local removal trial: relevant targeted test or script dry-run passes. Cite the exact command (e.g. `go test ./internal/benchmark/...`, `bash scripts/beadbench/<x>.sh --dry-run`). |
161	
162	Cast files, JSONL session captures, and old benchmark profiles are
163	typical candidates: they often outlive the experiment that produced them.
164	Verify whether a research note, doc, or test still references them before
165	classifying.
166	
167	## Inventory table template
168	
169	CL-002, CL-003, and CL-004 should each produce a table of this shape (or
170	several tables, one per area, if the candidate count warrants it). The
171	deletion beads (CL-005, CL-006, CL-007) cite the row by its `id` when
172	landing the change.
173	
174	| id | path | type | classification | reason | evidence | superseder / replacement | follow-up |
175	|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
176	| `CL-002.01` | `internal/foo/bar.go` | go-file | delete | no importers; symbol `Bar` unreferenced | `go list ./... ` clean; `rg '"…/internal/foo"'` empty; `rg '\bBar\b'` empty; `go test ./...` green after trial removal | — | — |
177	| `CL-003.07` | `docs/research/old-thing.md` | docs-research | archive | superseded by `docs/research/new-thing-2026-04-15.md`; one stale inbound link | `rg 'old-thing.md' docs/ website/` → only the stale link; that link is in a doc already marked obsolete | `docs/research/new-thing-2026-04-15.md` | move to `docs/research/archive/` and drop the stale inbound link in same commit |
178	| `CL-004.12` | `testdata/harness-cassettes/legacy-foo.json` | fixture | delete | no test loads it; cassette format superseded | `rg 'legacy-foo.json' .` empty; `rg 'harness-cassettes' .` shows only loaders for current cassettes | — | — |
179	
180	Column rules:
181	
182	- `id`: stable across the epic. Inventory beads assign these and they are
183	  cited verbatim by the deletion beads' commit messages.
184	- `classification`: exactly one of `delete`, `archive`, `keep`.
185	- `reason`: one short clause per row. If a `keep` row exists, give the
186	  category (e.g. "historical: HELIX retrospective", "active: imported by
187	  cmd/agentcli").
188	- `evidence`: list the actual commands and their outputs in summary form
189	  (e.g. `rg "<pkg>" empty`, `go test ./... pass`). The deletion bead
190	  re-runs these and cites them in its commit.
191	- `superseder / replacement`: required for any `superseded` row.
192	- `follow-up`: any side-effect the deletion bead must make in the same
193	  commit (drop a stale link, update an index, regenerate a `go.sum`).
194	
195	## Per-deletion checklist (used by CL-005 / CL-006 / CL-007)
196	
197	Before staging a deletion, the implementing bead **must** confirm each
198	item against the candidate row:
199	
200	- [ ] Inventory row exists, is classified `delete` or `archive`, and is
201	      cited by the bead's commit message.
202	- [ ] Re-run the row's evidence commands on `HEAD`; results still match.
203	      If they do not, requeue the row to inventory rather than deleting.
204	- [ ] No new references have appeared since the inventory landed
205	      (`rg` on the symbol/path/basename one more time).
206	- [ ] For Go: `go test ./...`, `go vet ./...`, lint pass after the
207	      deletion is staged.
208	- [ ] For docs: site build (if applicable) and any docs-link checks pass;
209	      no inbound link is left dangling.
210	- [ ] For scripts/fixtures/assets: targeted tests or dry-runs that touch
211	      the affected area pass.
212	- [ ] Commit stages only the intended files (`git add <paths>`, never
213	      `-A`), and the commit message subject ends with the candidate
214	      `id` from the inventory table.
215	- [ ] One commit per area split (the deletion beads' descriptions
216	      already require splitting by package/area; honor that).
217	
218	A deletion bead that cannot tick every box should classify the candidate
219	back to `keep` and document the blocker rather than ship a partial
220	deletion.
221	
222	## Rollback expectations
223	
224	Cleanup deletions must be cheaply reversible until the rename lands:
225	
226	1. **One commit per area, narrowly scoped.** Each deletion commit touches
227	   only one area (one Go package, one docs subtree, one fixture
228	   directory). A `git revert <sha>` on a single commit must be sufficient
229	   to bring the area back exactly as it was. No drive-by edits in
230	   deletion commits.
231	2. **No mixed concerns.** Cleanup commits do not perform renames, do not
232	   refactor, and do not rewrite unrelated docs. If a deletion exposes a
233	   refactor opportunity, file a follow-up bead.
234	3. **Pre-revert verification on `HEAD`.** The deletion-bead commit
235	   message records the exact verification commands it ran (`go test
236	   ./...`, lint, doc build, targeted script). On revert, those same
237	   commands are the regression check.
238	4. **Window for revert.** Deletions are revertible until CL-008 publishes
239	   the post-cleanup rename-surface count. Anything reverted after that
240	   point requires re-running CL-008.
241	5. **Archive is a `git mv`.** Archive commits use `git mv` so history is
242	   preserved across the move. A revert is `git mv` back; no content
243	   change.
244	6. **No deletions during the rename.** Once FZ-001 starts, the CL epic is
245	   closed. Late-discovered dead code is filed as a separate bead, not
246	   absorbed into a rename commit.
247	7. **Hard backstop.** If any post-deletion failure surfaces in CI, on a
248	   contributor's machine, or via a missing-fixture test failure, the
249	   default response is `git revert` first and re-classify the row to
250	   `keep` second. Do not patch forward under time pressure during the
251	   pre-rename window.
252	
253	## Out of scope
254	
255	CL-000 explicitly does **not** cover:
256	
257	- Renaming, repackaging, or moving live code.
258	- Refactors, even ones that would obviously help the rename.
259	- Editing historical HELIX or changelog artifacts to use new names.
260	- Cleaning up third-party submodules or vendored trees.
261	- Deleting issues, beads, or execution evidence under `.ddx/`.
262	
263	Anything that requires those is FZ work or a separate epic.

.PHONY: build build-ci install-quality-tools test test-no-race test-race lint vet fmt fmt-check gosec govulncheck ci-checks check clean coverage coverage-ratchet coverage-bump coverage-history catalog-dist

VERSION ?= $(shell git describe --tags --always --dirty 2>/dev/null || echo dev)
BUILD_TIME ?= $(shell date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
GIT_COMMIT ?= $(shell git rev-parse --short HEAD 2>/dev/null || echo unknown)
BINARY_NAME := ddx-agent
LDFLAGS := -ldflags "-X main.Version=$(VERSION) -X main.BuildTime=$(BUILD_TIME) -X main.GitCommit=$(GIT_COMMIT)"

build:
	go build $(LDFLAGS) -o $(BINARY_NAME) ./cmd/agent

catalog-dist:
	go run ./cmd/catalogdist \
		--manifest internal/modelcatalog/catalog/models.yaml \
		--out website/static/catalog \
		--channel stable \
		--min-agent-version "$${MIN_AGENT_VERSION:-$$(git describe --tags --abbrev=0 --match 'v*' 2>/dev/null || echo dev)}"

build-ci:
	go build ./...

install-quality-tools:
	go install github.com/golangci/golangci-lint/v2/cmd/golangci-lint@latest
	go install github.com/securego/gosec/v2/cmd/gosec@latest
	go install golang.org/x/vuln/cmd/govulncheck@latest

test:
	CGO_ENABLED=1 go test -race ./...

test-no-race:
	go test -count=1 ./...

test-race:
	CGO_ENABLED=1 go test -race -count=1 ./...

test-integration:
	CGO_ENABLED=1 go test -race -tags=integration ./...

test-e2e:
	CGO_ENABLED=1 go test -race -tags=e2e ./...

test-fuzz:
	go test -fuzz=. -fuzztime=30s ./...

lint:
	golangci-lint run

vet:
	go vet ./...

fmt:
	gofmt -l . | grep -v '^\.claude/' | grep -v '^\.ddx/' | grep . && exit 1 || true

fmt-check:
	@unformatted="$$(gofmt -l . | grep -v '^\.claude/' | grep -v '^\.ddx/')"; \
	if [ -n "$$unformatted" ]; then \
		echo "Files not formatted:"; \
		echo "$$unformatted"; \
		exit 1; \
	fi

gosec:
	gosec -exclude-dir=.claude -exclude-dir=.ddx ./...

govulncheck:
	govulncheck ./...

ci-checks: build-ci vet lint gosec govulncheck fmt-check test-no-race test-race
	@echo "All CI checks passed."

check: fmt vet lint test coverage-ratchet
	@echo "All checks passed."

# Coverage targets
coverage:
	go test -coverprofile=coverage.out ./...
	go tool cover -func=coverage.out
	@echo ""
	@echo "Full coverage report: coverage.html"
	go tool cover -html=coverage.out -o coverage.html

coverage-ratchet:
	@echo "Running coverage ratchet check..."
	@go run scripts/coverage-ratchet.go

coverage-bump: coverage-ratchet
	@echo "Auto-bumping coverage floors where coverage exceeds floor by >10%..."
	@go run scripts/coverage-ratchet.go --bump

coverage-history:
	@echo "Coverage history (from .helix-ratchets/coverage-floor.json):"
	@cat .helix-ratchets/coverage-floor.json | jq '.history'

coverage-trend: coverage-ratchet
	@echo "Coverage trend from history:"
	@go run scripts/coverage-ratchet.go --trend

clean:
	rm -f $(BINARY_NAME)
	go clean ./...

name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches: [master, main]
  pull_request:
    branches: [master, main]

jobs:
  test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v6

      - uses: actions/setup-go@v6
        with:
          go-version-file: go.mod

      - name: Install quality tools
        run: |
          make install-quality-tools
          echo "$(go env GOPATH)/bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"

      - name: Build
        run: make build-ci

      - name: Vet
        run: make vet

      - name: Lint
        run: make lint

      - name: Security scan
        run: make gosec

      - name: Vulnerability scan
        run: make govulncheck

      - name: Format check
        run: make fmt-check

      - name: Test
        run: make test-no-race

      - name: Test (race)
        run: make test-race
        if: runner.os == 'Linux'

    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v6

      - uses: actions/setup-python@v6
        with:
          python-version: "3.x"

      - name: Install pytest
        run: python -m pip install --upgrade pytest

      - name: Adapter pytest
        run: python -m pytest scripts/benchmark/harness_adapters
